sections.title: Civil Lawsuit
descriptions: Michael Anthony Roy filed a federal civil-rights lawsuit in June 2022 alleging that officers arrested him and used excessive force even after realizing he was not the person they were looking for. The parties settled for $93,000 without an admission of liability, and the case was dismissed with prejudice on December 8, 2022.

segments.text: The filing history for the federal lawsuit, from its June 24, 2022 filing through the dismissal with prejudice entered on December 8, 2022.
Roy alleges unlawful seizure, excessive force, failure to intervene, and related federal and state claims arising from his mistaken-identity arrest. These are allegations, not court findings.
The investigative report reviewing the arrest, the officers’ actions, and how information about Roy’s identity was communicated. It was filed as an exhibit to the complaint.
Photographs submitted with the complaint to document Roy’s alleged injuries.
The basic filing information submitted when the federal lawsuit was opened.
The agreement required the defendant parties to pay Roy a combined $93,000 in exchange for releasing his claims and dismissing the lawsuit. It states that no party admitted liability.
The November 15, 2022 agenda listed the Roy settlement agreement as a consent item recommended for approval.

descriptions: News coverage of Roy’s mistaken-identity arrest, alleged injuries, and federal lawsuit.

segments.text: Reporting on Roy’s account of being beaten and arrested even after officers learned they had the wrong person, along with the allegations in his lawsuit.
